_comment: Wall-clock seconds for one bats file in its own bats call on a GitHub windows-latest runner, Node 20. Used ONLY to balance CI shards -- never to gate anything. Stale numbers cost balance, never correctness: shard-tests.mjs asserts every file lands in exactly one shard whether or not it appears here.
_why: arc-ci's windows leg costs 1585s against ~145s on ubuntu for the same 563 tests -- 2.82s per test against 0.26s, because every bats `run` spawns a process and windows process creation is dear. Measured 2026-07-31 (run 30611012771): excluding the workspace and bats' binaries from Microsoft Defender changes nothing, because the runner image already ships with realtime protection OFF and both drives excluded. There is no windows-side saving left to find, so the fix stays splitting.
_provenance: Every one of the 104 files re-measured in a single pass on 2026-08-10 (run 31361908896, weigh-tests.yml, on feat/arc-leads-slice-06-fixes) -- one file per job, each timed in its own bats call with the scanners arc-ci installs. Re-run that workflow and paste its block rather than editing numbers by hand: a hand-picked weight is a guess wearing a measurement.
_evidence: The 2026-08-10 pass measured 47 files that had no entry at all and were riding _default_weight 16. The two this slice grew were among them and were badly wrong in the same direction: leads-journey.bats measured 111s and leads-mail-guard.bats 120s, i.e. roughly seven times their assumed weight, which is the shard imbalance H-04 describes. These weights are not asserted, they are checked. #73 shipped weights that predicted shard 7/12 at 111s; it ran 204s and then 198s, and it alone set the wall clock at 4m08. The re-measurement puts that shard's four files at 198s -- arc-scan 21->58, toolcheck 16->35, baseline 10->35, prune-report 64->70 -- which is the observed number, not a number near it. The 42 weights also now sum to 1593s against a real grouped windows total of 1585s measured independently, so the own-bats-call method predicts the invocation CI actually performs.
_floor: spine-emit.bats at 147s is now the floor no shard count can beat. design-steel-thread.bats, the previous floor at 141s, measured 128s in this pass -- the floor moved because the suite did, not because anything regressed. From 12 shards on, the heaviest shard IS that one file, and one file cannot be split across two runners.
_known_gap: UNMEASURED, AND COUNTED SO THE GAP IS VISIBLE RATHER THAN DEFAULTED: 3 file(s) -- absorb-ab-run.bats, absorb-rebuild-t01.bats, spine-worktree-guard.bats -- ride _default_weight 16. They arrived with the origin/main merge AFTER this weigh run was dispatched, so they are genuinely unmeasured rather than overlooked. lanes.md: a missing entry is a default rather than an error, so the count is stated here. These are WINDOWS seconds and the macOS leg is sharded with them, which is wrong in kind: the last 2-shard macOS split came out 77s and 161s against a prediction of 797/796, because the process-spawn cost that dominates windows does not dominate macOS. macOS is given a third shard to make the error small rather than a weights table of its own, since at 238s total it is not the binding leg. If it ever becomes one, weigh it on macos-latest instead of tuning the shard count.
